To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we fine-mapped the HOXB locus and identified a rare allele in HOXB13 that is a moderate risk factor for prostate cancer.

we identified a rare coding variant in the prostate cancer susceptibility gene HOXB13, G84E, that is tagged by common haplotypes and that the G84E allele associates with prostate cancer risk at high relative risk.

we have identified a novel common variant in the HOXA/C gene cluster that is associated with prostate cancer susceptibility and that this association is driven by the rare coding variant rs138213197 (G84E) in the HOXB 13 gene, which has been identified in recent studies as a moderate penetrant risk factor for prostate cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a rare coding region variant that has been shown to be associated with PrCa.

the clinical implications of genetic testing for G84E; if the G84E allele were incorporated into risk prediction algorithms for PrCa, it may be possible to improve the sensitivity for personalizing screening and prevention strategies for PrCa.
a rare coding variant (rs138213197), but its effect depends on much more common variants that are situated within or closely downstream of the HOXB13 locus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the G84E variant is likely to be the true causal locus in terms of the association with prostate cancer.
HOXB13 is the first rare variant of moderate risk for PrCa to be detected using a GWAS approach.
G84E and the common variants identified in this study (i.e. rs117576373) associate strongly with prostate cancer susceptibility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a common variant has been identified at a novel PrCa genetic locus, HOXB13, which is likely to be driven by a rare coding variant.

the HOXB13 locus is a rare coding variant example of a high penetrance susceptibility allele with a strong common SNP tag, with G×E interactions with prostate cancer risk factors providing a potential mechanism underlying this association.

a common variant in a promoter regulatory region (rs117576373) near HOXB13 is associated with PrCa susceptibility, and this association is likely driven by a low frequency coding variant (G84E) in HOXB13.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the rare allele, G, of rs138213197 should be included in risk prediction models for prostate cancer, and that the association between the common variant cluster and prostate cancer risk is probably due to linkage disequilibrium with this allele.

geneticists need to be aware that some of the most interesting and important associations identified in large-scale GWAS may be driven by rare variants that are not tagged by common variants in HapMap or 1000 Genomes.
geneticists need to be aware that some of the most interesting findings in future GWAS could originate from rare variants not present in reference samples.
